title: Williams Brothers Community Dinner:
title_short: Williams Brothers Community Dinner · Journey Recap
headline: Two NBA brothers and their mom bring their family's Sunday dinner to a family shelter, and a dad who lives there says it shows human kindness isn't dead.
story: The spine is a family ritual carried into a shelter: the dinner table, not the hardship. Jalen opens on Sunday dinner, Nicole tells where it comes from and what they bring: a fine-dining night that says <q>we're rooting and cheering for you</q>.
Jalen on giving back, Nicole on why CASS, then the people it was for: Ian, who lives at Vista Colina. The button is Nicole: there's still good in the world, <q>And that's us.</q>

Current fixes: music that starts slow and builds, the new CTA line on the end card after the logo animation, Nicole's name super (V3 showed Ian's name on her), supers lower, and captions always on under the supers.

[01:30.8] Not many people get to be in the position that we're in as far as just money and just being basketball players and doing what we love.

[01:42.6] It's something that our parents didn't let us take for granted.
[01:45.8] I feel like there's always somebody doing worse than you.
[01:48.2] So we always try to keep that in the back of our mind.
[01:50.4] And at the same time, just understanding where everybody comes from, I think that's a big one for me.
[01:55.6] Personally, everybody's going through their own thing.
[01:58.3] And we're all human.
[01:59.1] I think that, at the end of the day, is what makes this event special and what makes just our group, our surrounding, really special.

[02:25.8] Their main worry would be basketball practice.
[02:28.1] Like he said, there's always someone that's doing worse than you.
[02:30.9] So I feel like growing up, they always made sure that giving back and being part of the community and staying connected to God and giving back to those in the community and
[02:38.9] spreading the word of God was always just a big thing in our family.
[02:41.9] So being able to introduce that, coming and working with CASS.
[02:45.8] And like he said, people we've never met, being able to introduce that to them and kind of show them just the way we were growing up.
[02:52.0] I feel like that's a huge part of this.
[02:54.0] So being fortunate enough to be in this position to be able to give back is the biggest thing ever.
[02:58.4] Yeah, 100%.
[02:59.8] So what moment from tonight stood out to you all the most, would you say?
[03:03.6] The heat, for sure.
[03:04.4] I was sweating.
[03:05.8] A lot of people sweat in today's shirts.
[03:07.1] I would honestly say the fact that we were able to be as efficient as we were with the fact that it was really hot.
[03:12.8] But I think, and I think Cody would probably agree, the fact that it was that hot and everybody still had that good of a time just kind of lets you know the impact

[03:20.4] And I mean, obviously you'll probably say the same thing.
[03:23.7] Just like as hot as it was, it didn't feel that hot because everybody was having fun or talking, just bonding over just stuff.
[03:30.8] You know, we're eating.
[03:31.6] I think eating is almost like a sacred thing.
[03:34.6] Like you look back at the beginning of time, like everybody eats with each other.
[03:39.1] And it's like a sign of respect and endearment.
[03:41.4] And no matter how hot it was, it was just fun to be around everybody.
[03:46.9] Totally.
